source_text: ἁγίῳ ναῷ, τῷ ἐκ Παρθένου φημί· τὸν αὐτὸν δὴ τρόπον καὶ ἡ στάμνος ἡμῖν ἡ χρυσῆ, τὸ μάννα τὸ αἰσθητὸν ὠδίνουσα, τὸν ἄνωθεν καὶ ζωοποιὸν ἐμφαίνει Λόγον, δῆλον δὲ ὅτι τὸν ἐκ Πατρὸς, ὡς ἐν ἱερῷ καὶ ἀχράντῳ σώματι. Ἐπίμεστος δὲ καὶ ἡ στάμνος τοῦ
pass_a_gloss: …hagiō naō ek Parthenou… stamnos… plērōma theotētos sōmatikōs… Korē Dathan Abeirōn… dōdeka rhabdoi…
pass_b_english: Cyril: …holy temple, the one from Virgin I mean; in the same manner also the golden jar for us, travailing the sense-perceptible manna, shows the Word from above and life-making, clear that the one from Father, as in a holy and unstained body. And the jar also is filled full of the manna. ‘For in him all the fullness of the godhead has dwelt bodily,’ (Colossians 2:9) according at least to blessed Paul’s voice. ‘And not from measure does he give the Spirit.’ (John 3:34) For Christ is all-perfect. And the jar was set away, unto keeping unto the generations of the sons of Israel. For incorruptible and remaining always, and in every season and time most known is Christ. And he is opposite Lord—that is, in the eyes of the Father. For when the Only-begotten has come to be according to us, then also he has entered into the Holies of holies, through the greater and more perfect tent—that is, into the heaven, now to be manifested to the face of God for us, according as has been written. For he does not set himself in sight of the Father, but us as in himself, though having come to be from face and somehow as from eyes, through the transgression in Adam, and the sin that tyrannized over all. In Christ therefore we have had the approach, and the boldness unto the entrance of the Holies, just as wise Paul said to us. For just as also we have been raised together and seated together in the heavenly things in Christ, so again in him we have also come to be in face of the Father. And concerning the sacred jar let these things be said; and it signifies that Aaron’s rod also itself means Christ—come then let us say, if it seems good.

Cyril: Korah then and indeed also Abiram, and in addition to this Dathan, sprouted from tribe and blood of Levi; and having been entrusted, he says, with a liturgy arranged by the votes from above in the holy tent, they have thirsted for the glory of Moses and of Aaron, snatching the honor for themselves, though not having been called toward this by God. And indeed also priding themselves unto harsh boldness, and being very supercilious, they were making the abuse against both no longer bearable, but altogether hard to carry; and as untamed bulls they were separating themselves, and shaking off the slavery under God, they were persuading other impious ones to leap away together with them. But they were exacting justice of the things dared by them. For the earth opening its mouth was sending down into Hades the boastful people, with those of the same race, tents and properties; and wishing to make clear that by the vote from above, and not by Moses’ wills, Aaron has been allotted the excelling order in priesthood, the lawgiver said toward all-excellent Moses: ‘Speak to the sons of Israel, and take from them a rod, according to houses of families, from all their rulers, according to houses of their families, twelve rods, and of each write his name upon the rod. And Aaron’ (Hebrews 9:11–24)s name write upon the rod of Levi. For there is one rod. According to tribe of house of their families they will (Ephesians 2:6) (Numbers 17:2–3)
